What are Transformers?

Transformers are a type of neural network architecture, first introduced in 2017, that have revolutionized the field of natural language processing (NLP) and are also increasingly used in computer vision. They are particularly known for their ability to process long sequences of data, like text, by using a mechanism called "self-attention" which allows them to weigh the importance of different parts of the input relative to each other. This enables them to capture long-range dependencies in data much more effectively than previous architectures like recurrent neural networks (RNNs) or convolutional neural networks (CNNs).

tell me about transformer attention

Transformer attention is a mechanism introduced in the Transformer model that allows it to weigh the importance of different parts of the input sequence when processing each word or token. It helps the model focus on relevant information, capturing long-range dependencies efficiently. This is done by computing a score for how much each word in the input relates to the current word being processed, using Query, Key, and Value vectors. Multi-head attention allows the model to perform this focusing multiple times in parallel, capturing different aspects of relationships.
